title: Prospective cohort study on the impact of arthroscopically diagnosed concomitant injuries of the scapholunate ligament, lunotriquetral ligament, and triangular fibrocartilage complex on functional outcomes in patients with distal intra-articular radius fractures
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate how additional injuries to the ligaments of the wrist affect healing and wrist function after a wrist fracture. The study focuses on fractures of the radius, one of the two bones in the forearm, that extend into the wrist joint.
During surgery, the wrist joint is examined using a small camera in a procedure called wrist arthroscopy. This allows the surgeon to identify any additional ligament injuries. Patients will then attend regular follow-up visits. The study will compare the healing process in patients with and without these additional injuries. It will assess how well wrist function recovers and whether signs of wear and tear in the joint, known as osteoarthritis, develop over time.
In the long term, the results may help doctors tailor treatment more precisely and better estimate the chances of recovery for affected patients.
conditions: distal intra-articular fractures of the radius

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Age ≥ 18 years
-Acute, closed, intra-articular distal radius fracture confirmed by imaging
-Indication for surgical treatment with open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF)
-Capacity to provide informed consent and written consent to participate in the study and attend the follow-up examinations
Exclusion criteria:
-Open fractures
-Polytrauma with an Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) score ≥ 3 if adequate follow-up cannot be ensured
-Pre-existing symptoms and/or previous surgery involving the affected wrist, such as a known unstable scapholunate ligament injury, rheumatoid arthritis, or severe degenerative joint disease
-Neurological disorders resulting in permanent impairment of hand function
-Refusal to undergo arthroscopic examination
-Pregnancy
